steps: Implement a function that loads all .npz files from data/adbench/
Each file returns (X, y) where X is the feature matrix and y is binary (0=normal, 1=anomaly)
Verify all 57 datasets load without error
Print dataset name, shape, and anomaly ratio for each
Implement preprocessing compatible with tabular ADBench datasets
Handle mixed types: numerical scaling, categorical encoding
Handle missing values gracefully
Ensure preprocessing is fit only on training data to avoid leakage

description: Adapt anomaly detection model for tabular input
steps: Review current model pipeline and identify any assumptions about input format
Ensure model accepts 2D numpy arrays of shape (n_samples, n_features)
Ensure model outputs a 1D anomaly score array of shape (n_samples,)
Test on one ADBench dataset end-to-end
Implement compute_auroc(y_true, scores) using sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score
Handle edge cases: all-same labels, NaN scores
Write unit test with known inputs and expected AUROC output
Verify against a trivial detector (random scores should give ~0.5)
Iterate over all 57 ADBench datasets
For each: load data, preprocess, fit model, score, compute AUROC
Log each result with dataset name and AUROC
Handle failures gracefully: catch exceptions, log error, skip dataset
Save results to results/per_dataset_auroc.csv
Compute mean AUROC across all successfully evaluated datasets
Generate a results table: dataset name, n_samples, n_features, anomaly_ratio, AUROC
Sort by AUROC descending
Save to results/final_results.csv and print summary to stdout
Implement RFuni baseline from the BlackRock paper (arXiv 2504.16075)
RFuni: train RandomForest to distinguish real data from uniform synthetic data
Compute GAP distances, then use median distance to central 50% as anomaly score
Run RFuni on all 57 ADBench datasets and record AUROC
Save RFuni results to results/rfuni_baseline.csv
Load results/final_results.csv and results/rfuni_baseline.csv
Merge on dataset name
Compute per-dataset delta (our model AUROC - RFuni AUROC)
Compute mean AUROC for both models
Print comparison table and highlight datasets where we outperform / underperform RFuni
Save to results/comparison.csv
Create results/ directory if it does not exist
Set random seeds for all stochastic components (numpy, sklearn)
Log Python and package versions to results/env_info.txt
Ensure full pipeline can be re-run from scratch and produces identical results
Create run_evaluation.py that executes the full pipeline in one command
Steps: load data → preprocess → fit/score → evaluate → compare to RFuni → print summary
Add --dataset flag to run on a single dataset for quick testing
Add --baseline-only flag to run just RFuni for comparison
Verify python run_evaluation.py completes without errors
